rounds.text: Narmada Gelatines presents a compelling value opportunity, trading at a P/E of 8.54x [E1] and an EV/EBITDA of 6.13x against a sector benchmark of 11.69x [E11], which underpins a DCF intrinsic value of Rs 1314 per share [E35] and a 62.6% margin of safety [E36]. This valuation discount exists despite remarkable capital efficiency, highlighted by a ROCE of 29.5% [E12] against a sector benchmark of 9.76% [E10] and an ROE of 23.7% [E13] against a sector benchmark of 8.17% [E9]. The company's underlying earnings power is demonstrated by trailing twelve-month profit growth of 81% [E15], quarterly operating margin expansion to 21% [E21], and Rs 15 Cr in free cash flow [E26]. Balance sheet risk is minimal as the business is conservatively financed with a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x [E28] and reduced borrowings of Rs 8 Cr [E30], while benefiting from a tailwind in the chemical sector [E59]. Operational upside is further supported by expanding gelatin applications in pharmaceutical and nutraceutical markets [E63, E64] alongside active energy-efficiency measures [E66, E67]. Conceded: sourcing quality crushed bone raw materials remains a major concern [E74], plant-based substitutes pose market obstacles [E73], and promoter shareholding dropped 2.65 percentage points to 75.00% [E32]. Nevertheless, with current pricing implying an earnings contraction of -3.8% [E37] despite the company scoring 85 out of 100 on a rules-based screen [E51], the stock remains significantly under-appreciated.
